summary: Rota Fácil MVP first-round testing. Backend: 13/13 pytest tests PASS (100%) - root metadata, parse-text BR/MLB codes, parse-file CSV/TXT, geocode-batch (Nominatim ~1s/addr), optimize TSP (validated nearest-neighbor ordering), PIX generate (EMV-compliant BR Code with CNPJ 48223054000142, prefix 00020101021226, CRC16 footer 6304+hex), PIX confirm activates 30-day subscription persisted to MongoDB, subscription days_remaining ~29-30 verified. Frontend: Landing/Paywall/Upload/Route/Scanner screens render with all testIDs; manual route creation (BR + MLB codes) processed through /api/parse-text + /api/geocode-batch and navigated to /route; stop activation, active widget, menu modal (6 items), manual code locate, mark delivered (counter 2→1), optimize TSP, scanner web fallback all work. ISSUE: On RN Web, Alert.alert button onPress callback after confirmPayment never fires so router.replace('/') never runs — user is stranded on /paywall after clicking 'Já paguei' (API does succeed and subscription is activated server-side; works on native iOS/Android). ISSUE: react-native-webview shows 'React Native WebView does not support this platform.' on web preview — Leaflet map is invisible on web (works on native).

ui_bugs.issue: On RN Web, Alert.alert([{text:'Começar', onPress: ()=>router.replace('/')}]) does NOT invoke the onPress callback (RN Web maps Alert to window.alert which has no per-button callbacks). After successful confirmPayment, user stays on /paywall with no navigation. Subscription IS active on backend, but UX is broken on web. Fix: call router.replace('/') directly after await confirmPayment(...) and show Alert (or a Toast) separately, e.g. on native only.

react-native-webview is unsupported on web — page shows literal text 'React Native WebView does not support this platform.' near top of map area. Consider Platform.OS === 'web' fallback (iframe/leaflet directly, or a placeholder message styled as part of UI). On native this works; on web preview the map is missing.

react_native_issues.issue: Package version mismatches reported by Expo on startup: expo@54.0.34 (expected ~54.0.35), expo-font@14.0.11 (expected ~14.0.12), expo-router@6.0.23 (expected ~6.0.24). Run `npx expo install --check` (or update package.json) for full compatibility.

Add Platform.OS === 'web' fallback for the Leaflet map in route.tsx (e.g., embed Leaflet via an <iframe> or render the HTML inside a <View> using react-native-web's createElement, or show a styled placeholder). Currently web users see raw error text.
Update Expo packages to matching versions: `cd /app/frontend && npx expo install expo expo-font expo-router` (or pin versions in package.json).
Replace deprecated 'shadow*' style props with 'boxShadow' and 'props.pointerEvents' with 'style.pointerEvents' to silence warnings.

rca_of_issue: Bug RCA — Paywall stuck after 'Já paguei' on web: react-native-web's Alert.alert is implemented as window.alert(message) — it ignores the buttons array entirely and never calls onPress. Therefore router.replace('/') inside the 'Começar' button callback never executes on web. Reproduction: open /paywall, click 'Já paguei — Ativar Assinatura', observe URL stays at /paywall and no Start Route button appears (although /api/pix/confirm returns 200 and subscription is active in DB). Mitigation: navigate first, then alert — e.g. `await confirmPayment(...); router.replace('/'); Alert.alert('Assinatura Ativada! 🎉', '...');` — or use a custom in-app success modal/toast for cross-platform parity.
